c: Sculpture is the branch of the visual arts that operates in three dimensions. Sculpture is the three-dimensional artwork which is physically presented in the dimensions of height, width and depth. It is one of the plastic arts. Durable sculptural processes…
def: Sculpture is the branch of the visual arts that operates in three dimensions.

t: Visual art of Hong Kong
c: Hong Kong was a British colony from 1842 to 1997. The local art organizations were mostly run by Westerners who outnumbered Chinese painters until a large migration of Chinese from Southern China during Sino–Japanese War.
def: The visual art of Hong Kong, or Hong Kong art, refers to all forms of visual art in or associated with Hong Kong throughout its history and towards the present.

t: Taiwanese art
c: Many Chinese artists went to study western art in Paris in the early 1900s, for example: Fang Ganmin (方幹民), Wu Dayu (吳大羽), Ong Schan Tchow (翁占秋), Lin Fengmian (林風眠), Yan Wenliang (顏文樑), Wu Guanzhong (吳冠中), Zao Wou-Ki (趟無極).
def: The artistic heritage of Taiwan is extremely diverse with multiple major influences and periods.

t: Lacquerware
c: Excavations of Chu tombs have found painted wooden sculptures, jade disks, glass beads, musical instruments, and an assortment of lacquerware.
def: Lacquerware are objects decoratively covered with lacquer.

t: Landscape painting
c: Because pure landscape paintings are hardly seen in Europe until the 17th century, Strolling About In Spring may well be the world's first landscape painting.
def: Landscape painting, also known as landscape art, is the depiction in painting of natural scenery such as mountains, valleys, rivers, trees, and forests, especially where the main subject is a wide view—with its elements arranged into a coherent composition.

t: Visual arts
c: The visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture. Many artistic disciplines such as performing arts, conceptual art, and textile arts also…
def: The visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture.

t: Islamic world
c: Beyond East Asia, Chinese art shaped painting and ceramics in the Islamic world, and in Europe imported porcelain, lacquer and silk prompted local imitations, as well as the eighteenth-century fashion for chinoiserie in furniture, interiors and garden…
def: The terms Islamic world and Muslim world commonly refer to the Islamic community, which is also known as the Ummah.

t: Decorative arts
c: Decorative arts are extremely important in Chinese art, and much of the finest work was produced in large workshops or factories by essentially unknown artists, especially in Chinese ceramics, where technical mastery served broader aesthetic ideals, subtlety…
def: The decorative arts are arts or crafts whose aim is the design and manufacture of objects that are both beautiful and functional.

t: Shan shui
c: In contrast, the tradition of ink wash painting, practiced mainly by scholar-officials and court painters especially of landscapes, flowers, and birds, developed aesthetic values depending on the individual imagination of and objective observation by the…
def: Shan shui or shanshui refers to a style of traditional East Asian painting derived from Chinese painting that involves or depicts scenery or natural landscapes, using a brush and ink rather than more conventional paints.

t: Silk Road
c: Native Chinese religions do not usually use cult images of deities, or even represent them, and large religious sculpture is nearly all Buddhist, dating mostly from the 4th to the 14th century, and initially using Greco-Buddhist models arriving via the Silk…
def: The Silk Road was a network of Asian trade routes active from the second century BCE until the mid-15th century.

t: Famille rose
c: Jar: 18th century; porcelain painted in overglaze famille rose enamels; height: 61 cm; Metropolitan Museum of Art
def: Famille rose is a style of decoration in Chinese porcelain introduced in the 18th century and defined by pink overglaze enamel as the dominant colour.

t: Korean art
c: Chinese art exerted a major influence on the arts of Korea, Japan and Vietnam, which adopted and adapted a wide range of its forms, from calligraphy, painting and sculpture to architecture and city planning, garden design, ceramics, lacquerware, furniture,…
def: Korean arts include traditions in calligraphy, music, painting and pottery, often marked by the use of natural forms, surface decoration and bold colors or sounds.

t: Yungang Grottoes
c: Colossal seated Buddha, Cave 20, Yungang Grottoes, Datong, Shanxi. Northern Wei dynasty (5th century)
def: The Yungang Grottoes, formerly the Wuzhoushan Grottoes, are ancient Chinese Buddhist temple grottoes built during the Northern Wei dynasty near the city of Datong, then called Pingcheng, in the province of Shanxi.

t: Guanyin
c: Seated Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara (Guanyin), wood and pigment, 11th century, Chinese Northern Song dynasty, St. Louis Art Museum
def: Guanyin is a common Chinese name of the Bodhisattva associated with compassion known as Avalokiteśvara.

t: Penjing
c: Penjing, also known as penzai, is the ancient Chinese art of depicting artistically formed trees, other plants, and landscapes in miniature.
def: Penjing, also known as penzai, is the ancient Chinese art of depicting artistically formed trees, other plants, and landscapes in miniature.

t: Chinese opera
c: Traditional Chinese opera, or Xiqu, is a form of musical theatre in China with roots going back to the early periods in China. It is an amalgamation of various art forms that existed in ancient China, and evolved gradually over more than a thousand years,…
def: Traditional Chinese opera, or Xiqu, is a form of musical theatre in China with roots going back to the early periods in China.

t: Chinese martial arts
c: Chinese martial arts, commonly referred to with umbrella terms kung fu, kuoshu or wushu, are multiple fighting styles that have developed over the centuries in China. These fighting styles are often classified according to common traits, identified as…
def: Chinese martial arts, commonly referred to with umbrella terms kung fu, kuoshu or wushu, are multiple fighting styles that have developed over the centuries in China.

t: Guqin
c: A music instrument called Qin-zither was developed during the Qin dynasty. The aesthetic components have always been as important as the functional parts on a musical instrument in Chinese history.
def: The qin, or later guqin after the 20th century, is a plucked seven-string Chinese musical instrument.

t: Zhan Ziqian
c: Zhan Ziqian was a painter during the Sui dynasty. His only painting in existence is Strolling About In Spring arranged mountains perspectively.
def: Zhan Ziqian was a famous painter of ancient China from Yangxin County in modern-day Shandong province.

t: Qilin
c: Bronze statuette of a qilin, 1st century AD
def: The qilin is a legendary hooved chimerical creature that appears in Chinese mythology, and is said to appear with the imminent arrival or death of a sage or illustrious ruler.

t: Buddhist art
c: Monumental stone statuary would become a major art form from the 4–6th centuries CE with the onset of monumental Buddhist sculpture in China.
def: Buddhist art is visual art produced in the context of Buddhism.

t: Landed gentry in China
c: This is a large horizontal handscroll of a domestic scene showing men of the gentry class being entertained by musicians and dancers while enjoying food, beverage, and wash basins provided by maidservants.
def: The gentry, or landed gentry in China was the elite who also held additional privileged status through passing the Imperial exams, which made them eligible to hold government office.

t: Tuanshan
c: Circular-fan painting by Ma Lin
def: Tuanshan, also called gongshan, bian mian, fan of reunion, are typically silk rigid hand fan which originated in China.

t: Folding screen
c: Folding screens (Chinese: 屏風; pinyin: píngfēng) are often decorated with beautiful art; major themes include mythology, scenes of palace life, and nature.
def: A folding screen, also known as pingfeng, is a type of free-standing furniture consisting of several frames or panels, which are often connected by hinges or by other means.

t: Ding ware
c: Ding ware pillow in the shape of a recumbent child, Northern Song dynasty (12th century).
def: Ding ware, Ting ware or Dingyao are Chinese ceramics, mostly porcelain, that were produced in the prefecture of Dingzhou in Hebei in northern China.

t: Carved lacquer
c: Qing furniture retained the basic forms and joinery of the Ming but became far more richly decorated, with relief and openwork carving, inlays of mother-of-pearl, jade, enamel and stone, and carved lacquer.
def: Carved lacquer or Qidiao is a distinctive Chinese form of decorated lacquerware.
